steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: Federico... Federico! You're walking too fast! Please, wait up!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What's the matter, Trainee Roberto?

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: C'mon, why are you acting so cold? Didn't we both report in to the Notarial Hall on the same day? We're practically destined to become best buds, aren't we?

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: I promised Ranieri that I'd visit his sweets shop after work to have some pudding. You should come too!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That is an agreement between you and Trainee Ranieri. There's no need to involve me.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Also, please remove your hand from my shoulder. Excessive physical contact interferes with the efficiency of my work.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: What work...? Oh, are you talking about the investigation we just did of the Pagus Stevonus Central Hospital?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That would be the only item on our list of outstanding tasks.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: But didn't the doctor say that everyone involved in the accident came down with some disease?

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: Something went wrong with the patients' collective empathy... While that's tragic, we're executors, not medics, and there's not a whole lot we can do.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I've already reviewed the hospital records. Diseases related to the loss of collective empathy are extremely rare, with only seven recorded cases. Whereas in the past three days, we've received fifteen patients with the exact same symptoms across the various districts.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Statistical anomalies like this cannot be ignored.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: So you suspect they're not actually sick? Then, what do you think is causing all this? Ha, you don't think there's some weirdo out there purposefully stuffing their heads full of emotions that don't belong to them, do you?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It is certainly one possibility.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: ...I was just kidding.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I would need to do more research before making any further conjectures.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: Alright then. Sounds like you won't be enjoying yourself with us. I can get a few muffins for you though – what flavor do you... Hey, would it kill you to stop walking so fast?!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...And that is the general outline of the case.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: As you are a famous neurosurgeon, I am here to ask for your professional opinion.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Is there any way to artificially interfere with the collective empathy between Sankta?

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Interfering with our collective empathy... *cough*, *cough*! Fede, what you speak of is utterly impossible. Our empathy is a miracle unique to our race. Who could possibly hope to pry it wide open?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...Impossible?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Understood. Thank you for sharing your professional input.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: As always, I brought some food, and will leave it in the fridge.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...The fridge is full. I'll dump out some of the expired food before I leave.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: I know how busy you are with work. You don't have to keep visiting me all the time.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The curtains are drawn open.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: The curtains? *cough*, *cough* That was me. I went out a bit, earlier in the day. Why?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Avuncle, I don't have classes right now, and can stay for up to a week.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I was planning on clearing up some of the clutter in the living room today. I learned some Arts for quickly crushing hard objects that should prove useful in a large cleanup.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Out of consideration for the possible noise, I'd advise you to stay inside. I'll relocate any of your valuables, so...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...It's gone.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: What's gone?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The cello. Arturia always kept it by the window. Now, the curtains are drawn open and the cello is gone.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Did she leave?

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: ...I let her go.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: I sent her to Leithanien. She's had so many teachers anyway, and they've all praised her 'gift.'

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Hah. 'Gift'! The damn thing ruined your aunt, the woman I loved!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You still can't accept her.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: How could I? Whenever I see her, whenever I hear her music... I'm reminded of the pain of losing a loved one.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Mm. The pain you feel has even started to affect your physical health.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Fede, you have no idea how much I envy you. Do you not miss the people who've passed on? Like your aunt, or your parents?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I remember every detail of the time I spent with them.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: But do you ever go crazy thinking about how much you miss them? Do you ever feel regret for not spending your time with them more meaningfully?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Mater taught me that if I always make the best possible choice in the moment, then there is nothing to regret.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: ...Which is why I envy you. Because her music won't affect you.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Ha. It goes beyond that though, child. I envy you and your lack of empathy. I envy you for not becoming addicted to emotions, let alone regret.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Based on what I see, you've already started to regret your latest decision.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You know full well that Leithanien's synthesis of musical and Arts talent will only serve to further strengthen Arturia's Arts.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: During the funeral, she made everyone who heard her music recall my aunt, and in the process revealed their hidden emotions.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Fortunately, everyone's lives returned to normal after the performance. Aside from some embarrassing memories, her music did not cause any lasting harm.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But that may not be the case next time. When she returns to Laterano, her special 'gift' may cause even greater turmoil.
Even greater turmoil.
For example, some low-probability events that would otherwise never happen.
Federico looks to the window. Indeed, there is no longer a cello casting its shadow beside it.
But Federico's memory never errs. For the last four years, Marcello had never opened the curtains, no matter how bright the sun was outside.
To be more precise, he found it unbearable to even approach the place where the cello once rested.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: When I told you about the case, I did not mention that it was an 'empathetic expansion' incident.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You don't have to answer the questions I am about to ask, but know that I will also interpret your silence as an answer.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Avuncle Marcello, has Arturia been here recently?

steps.name: Hospital Careworker
steps.text: Seniora, the test results have all come back. Your nerves are a bit overstimulated right now, but otherwise, there's nothing particularly wrong with your body.

steps.name: Hospital Careworker
steps.text: But you're still not willing to talk?

steps.name: Hospital Careworker
steps.text: Those two... Err, no, that one young executor came by again.

steps.name: Hospital Careworker
steps.text: He keeps asking to see you, but he's... a bit too blunt. The doctor is worried that his brusque manner will disrupt your mental state again, just when we've finally gotten your mood to stabilize.

steps.name: Hospital Careworker
steps.text: Uhh, what's this... a slip of paper? He slipped a note under the door with a name written on it.

steps.name: Hospital Careworker
steps.text: 'Arturia.' What's that supposed to mean?

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: ...*gasp*!

steps.name: Hospital Careworker
steps.text: Wh-Why are you so agitated all of a sudden?! Should I call the doctor?

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: No... I'd like to meet with him.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Hello.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: ...I can't feel you.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If you mean that your empathy did not alert you to my presence, then that is not due to any empathetic imbalance on your part, but rather a problem with me.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: Did you cut yourself off from our collective empathy, or do you suffer from some deficiency?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The professionals lean towards it being physiological.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: Poor child.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: You'll never know... what you are lacking.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I appreciate your concern, but I've come to the conclusion that I am perfectly capable of performing my duties.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Moving on, I'd like to ask you a direct question – have you met with Arturia Giallo recently?

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: ...I have.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: I saw her. No, more than that... I heard her. I heard her performing.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I can infer that she was performing at the church where you worked. Everyone who attended service that day heard her play.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: I was conducting a sermon that day.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Did you know Arturia beforehand?

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: ...No. That was my first time meeting her.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: She sat in the corner of the front row, listened to the entire sermon, then asked me a question.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Please state the question in question.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: She asked me...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You just asked us to close our eyes and feel the emotions of our fellow countrymen sitting beside us.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: So I did.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I felt... bathed in peace and joy, just like every moment I spend in Laterano City.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But Seniora, I can't help but wonder, what of that day five years ago?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: When those refugees, displaced by war, came to our doorsteps after crossing the wilderness, only to be ignored by you. Did you feel the pain in their hearts?

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: What... are you talking about?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It seems that your memories have faded with time. Allow me to help you recall.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Among them were children and the elderly. Feline and Liberi. And also... several Sankta who'd been born elsewhere.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: They journeyed here under the guidance of a kind-hearted individual, believing that someone in Laterano would help them.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But the hopes of those poor souls were shattered. It didn't take long for most of them to perish in the sands.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: ...And you wish to take revenge on me on their behalf, child?

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: Because of my fear of Oripathy, because of my inability to empathize with their suffering.... You've come here to expose me, to shame me?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: No, Seniora. I have no right to retaliate against you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And as long as your actions match the emotions deep in your heart... I won't even judge you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But you are supposed to be a kind person. Please tell me – is the reason you refused to help those people because you've grown accustomed to our collective empathy, but are unable to truly feel the emotions of others?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And I pose the same question to every person sitting here.
Arturia stands up and walks into the crowd.
She pauses and stops in front of each and every Sankta, feeling their thoughts as if they were the most intimate friends.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You blew up a flowerbed this morning. Do you feel for the others living in the same neighborhood, who are now mourning the loss of a precious childhood memory?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And you, you were in a hurry to get home yesterday, and rushed to board the public transit. Do you feel for the elderly woman you pushed aside, who was herself anxious about not being able to get to the hospital in time?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I am the same.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It is not that we were born selfish, weak, or dishonest.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We simply hid beneath our Sankta halos, using our 'collective empathy' as both the premise and expression of mutual care, and deemed that to be enough.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But can we truly accept another person's emotions as our own?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Did you answer her question?

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: I had no way of answering.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: She posed that question to everyone present.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: And afterward, she asked us, 'would you like to feel even more?'

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: She walked to the center of the church, lifted her bow, and began to perform... our hymn.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: It's not as if she took control of us. But we were all drawn to the sound of her cello.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: I had heard the same hymn countless times before, but in that moment, it was as if I was hearing its melody for the very first time.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: The whole city... blossomed to life in my mind.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You're crying tears of happiness.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: That's right. Even now, I can still feel those effervescent emotions.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: Some are crying, others are laughing; some are born, others pass away.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: The doctors called my symptoms an 'empathy disorder.' They said that the memories I was seeing were deranged hallucinations, and wanted me to take tranquilizers.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: But only I know... No, only those of us who heard that hymn know.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: None of us had ever 'felt' each other before. Or 'felt' Laterano, or 'felt' the advent, continuation, and cessation of life as we did in that moment.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: Under the torrent of such powerful emotions, I no longer feel shame or regret towards what I did in the past.

steps.name: Silent Cleric
steps.text: I know clearly that their pain will become my pain, and I will carry those memories with me as my own, until I face my next decision.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Thank you for your cooperation. I will report your testimony to the Notarial Hall.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: Where are you, Federico?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Roberto, as you are my partner, I have an obligation to inform you of my intentions.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am ordering the arrest of Arturia, the suspect in the 'empathetic expansion' case. She is most likely in the cemetery right ahead of me.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have already sent you the coordinates. Please be prepared to cooperate.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: G-Giallo? Isn't she your...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Distant relative. But that has no bearing on my decision-making.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You're here alone again, Soror.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Avuncle has also locked himself inside. The two of you haven't spoke in a long time.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why not tell him that you're suffering?

steps.name: Calm Voice
steps.text: There's no point.

steps.name: Calm Voice
steps.text: Fede, my father's love for my mother blinded him to her true emotions. He wanted nothing but to keep her by his side, but she didn't want to be chained down by him.

steps.name: Calm Voice
steps.text: I only wanted to help him realize this, but he pushed me away.

steps.name: Calm Voice
steps.text: He would rather hate me than admit that it was Mamma's idea to leave him.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Regardless, you shouldn't have caused such a commotion at the funeral.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: People are hurt by your music. I agree with Avuncle's judgment that you were in the wrong.

steps.name: Calm Voice
steps.text: Are you also afraid of me, Fede? Just like father, and everyone else at that funeral?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...I'm not afraid of you.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But...
The Sankta girl stands silently before a tombstone.
She continues playing her cello, each note filled with emotions that Federico cannot feel.
All he can do is sit on the grass not far away, scrawling away and thinking, occasionally lifting his head to look at the tightly-shut windows, the vibrating strings, and the silent tombstones.
He can even discern that the sound of the cello reverberating in the wind is becoming more and more frantic.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I will stop you.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I will not allow you to continue your self-centered performance—

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: —Arturia.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It's been a while, Fede.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Are you also here to pay a visit to Mamma?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You know why I'm here.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You're still exactly the same as when you were little. Always so straightforward... always so good at spoiling the mood.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Three days ago, in a church in Pagus Stevonus, you used Originium Arts on thirty-one Sanktas, causing them to suffer from an empathy disorder in serious violation of our laws.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: As an executor of the Notarial Hall, I declare you under arrest.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Did you know? Ever since you were little, I always knew you'd grow up to be an exemplary executor.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But... Well, even I couldn't imagine that I'd be the first person you tried to arrest.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: From a certain perspective, that makes this rather amusing, doesn't it?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Federico Giallo and Arturia Giallo were born to be mortal enemies.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I do not find that amusing.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your actions seriously threaten the stability of Laterano.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Fede, do you know why I went to that church?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The refugees abandoned by the clerics were rescued from the battlefield by a Sankta named Luciana.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That's right. I wanted to see where my mother went after she left Laterano, so I retraced the path she took and found the people she'd helped.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: One of these places happened to be a settlement, where my mother described the beauty of Laterano to them. She told them to come here for help in desperate times.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: She knew that most of them were Infected, and would not be accepted by the pure Holy City. But she thought that her handwritten letter would impress her former friends and colleagues.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But what she didn't know was that most of them would treat her ideals—her feelings—as a laughingstock at her funeral.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Even the few who still held good feelings towards her... such as that cleric, would go on to look away from the plight of others.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That does not justify harming her or any of the others present.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Harming them?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I simply allowed them to share each other's emotions.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: After that, they gained the opportunity to become brave, benevolent, and compassionate people, just as Mamma was.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You speak of something completely uncertain and absolutely beyond your control.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The indiscriminate expansion of the scope of Sankta empathy will affect our daily lives, causing uncontrollable panic and chaos.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The order that people are accustomed to would cease to exist, to the point where it would become dangerous to leave one's home. Law-breaking behavior will occur on a massive scale, which may trigger a large number of Sankta falling from grace in a short period of time.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: While becoming kinder is one possibility, they may also become violent or crazed, or even turn into criminals who threaten public safety.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I see that you can't accept that the order you're so familiar with has long since lost its rationality.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Look at the truth. Emotions alone never give rise to madness. On the contrary, it is only when your heart cannot accept your own emotions that they pierce the shield of reason.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We should have broken away from this false order constraining our emotions, making people callous, hypocritical, and cowardly.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Only afterwards can a new, emotion-driven life be truly built. We'll be more free... and have less regrets.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It is unclear who you are referring to as 'we,' as well as the context of 'afterwards.'

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: All I know is that, much like Amita Luciana – your mother – it has no future.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Fede, you really know how to hit someone where it hurts.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I know it wasn't your intention, but... you made me feel pain so effortlessly.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Oftentimes, pain can be a wake-up call.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: However, judging from your subsequent actions, I cannot tell if you've ever experienced even a moment of remorse.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Remorse?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If there's anything I regret, it's that I couldn't do more for my mother at the time. So she wouldn't been so easily and hastily taken by death while on the path to realizing her innermost feelings.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your choice is irrational.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Fede, how I wish you could understand the sound of my music.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: How I wish I could share with you what I think and feel when I stand in front of my mother's tombstone, recalling those times over and over again.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I refuse. No amount of emotions justify your crimes.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I don't want to exonerate myself. I just... want you to understand me.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Put down your cello. I won't allow you to touch those strings anymore.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: My beloved brother, are you really going to point your gun at me?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Unless you decide to surrender yourself.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You and I both know that's not possible.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia, I cannot allow any enemies of Laterano to move freely about the Holy City unsanctioned.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The sound of your music may not affect me, but the same cannot be said for others nearby.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I can no longer allow you to weave your illusions, to fill the minds of others with your unnecessary emotions, or even shake the very foundations of our collective empathy.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You... refer to the very real memories my music brings people as the complete opposite, 'illusions.' Why? You've certainly never denied the meaning of emotions to yourself.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I really ought to hate you, Federico...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But still, seeing how we've been apart for so long, I've prepared a gift to celebrate our reunion.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Look over there.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: A vendor's car?

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: There you are, Federico!

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: I have no idea why, but a few youngsters kept trying to drag me along, saying they wanted to turn this place into a venue for a balloon contest and needed an executor there to certify it...

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa... What are you doing?

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: Why are you pointing your gun at another Sankta? Are you trying to fall?

spans.text: Why are you pointing your gun at another Sankta? Are you

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That's not a matter worth consideration in our current situation.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: I can't let you do this!

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: You said that you were looking for Arturia Giallo, right? She's your sister! I know there might be some history between you two, but don't be rash!
The speeding balloon car shows no signs of stopping.
Federico springs forward, grabs the two people from the left and right sides of the vehicle as quickly as possible, and throws them onto the grass.
Countless balloons fly out of the car. The sudden kaleidoscope of colors blots out the sky as well as his vision. Though it lasted but a brief moment, it was enough.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: She got away.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Please take the people who were in the car just now, and report to Pagus Stevonus Central Hospital together.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: You still have things to investigate? I thought you already got to the bottom of the case!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I'd suggest you undergo a full-body checkup.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Just now, you might all have been affected by the sound of Arturia's cello.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: I don't feel any different...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Assuming you haven't been affected, I have another suggestion.

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Executor-in-Training
steps.text: Oh! I know – you're about to suggest that I find myself a new job, right? Well shoot, I was just thinking the same thing! I knew we were destined to be best buds!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...And that is how my meeting with Arturia went.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Apologies, Avuncle Marcello, but I've already submitted the evidence to the Notarial Hall.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It is said that several cardinals have personally reviewed the files and identified Arturia as a wanted individual.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: My child, you... made the correct decision. The one I couldn't bring myself to make.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: I keep thinking, what if I hadn't sent Arturia away... What if I hadn't closed myself off to Luciana's emotions when I learned of her death...

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Would she not have gone further down her misguided path?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: There's no point speculating.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: All I know is that it was Arturia Giallo's own choice to embark on the chaotic path she currently walks.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: And that I will personally see to it that she is brought to justice, and made to face the consequences of her actions.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: They asked you to arrest your own sister?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am the most qualified.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Not only because I am one of the few unaffected by her music... But also, even if she herself is unwilling to admit it, there's a good chance that nobody in all of Laterano knows her better than I do.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: What happens after you arrest her? Will the law... sentence her?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: According to the records, Laterano's laws have been supplemented and amended countless times in the millennium since the city's founding.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Considering the uniqueness of Arturia's Arts, the crimes she committed may be difficult to prosecute under our current laws—

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But as long as she continues to pose an objective threat, the gun of an executor will continue to render correct judgments.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: You're only a kid... You just graduated.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Do you think that I am incapable of taking on such a large responsibility?

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Hah... If anything, I'm worried that you're a bit too responsible. Federico, I'm sure you'll become one of Laterano's best executors, just like your parents.

spans.text: Hah... If anything, I'm worried that you're a bit
responsible. Federico, I'm sure you'll become one of Laterano's best executors, just like your parents.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Maybe... I really am getting old. Recently, I keep thinking back to the past.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Not long after your parents passed away, when you first came to our house. Luciana was still with us, and you and Arturia were such lovely children. We'd get together to have water gun fights, and...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If that is your heart's desire, I can take half a day off to play with you.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Haha. You really are a good kid.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Actually, there is one thing... that you yourself might not have made sense of.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: You say that Arturia hates you because you deny the meaning of emotion.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: But it might just be that she knows you better than you know yourself.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Please elaborate.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Federico, you're the most sincere and open child I've ever met. You never run from your past, and you never suppress any of your emotions.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: You've left Arturia at a complete loss... along with her Arts.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I find myself somewhat puzzled at your statement.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Then every once in a while, just stop thinking.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: So, come on in and let your uncle give you a hug, okay?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This request for physical contact makes me...
The door that had been closed for eight years was open.
The curtains were never closed again, revealing window panes as clean and clear as the blue sky.
On the table are several muffins and a glass of steaming water.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...A hug is an acceptable request.
